findings.text: Operations setup_boot_APIC_clock and setup_secondary_APIC_clock plus query apic_needs_pit and workaround amd_e400_c1e_apic_setup are externally reachable initialization services.
Operations clear_local_APIC and apic_soft_disable plus disable_local_APIC and lapic_shutdown are externally reachable lifecycle services for masking, soft disable, full disable and safe shutdown.

Operations sync_Arb_IDs and apic_intr_mode_select plus init_bsp_APIC and apic_intr_mode_init and disable_ioapic_support are externally reachable configuration services for arbitration, mode choice, early setup and IO APIC control.

Timer system vector acts as an interrupt entry that acknowledges the controller, preserves caller register context across handling, brackets work with entry and exit tracing, then hands off to per processor timer dispatch.

Timer calibration records countdown and power timer and jiffies at start and end boundaries, adding time stamp counter samples when that feature is present, with end power timer compensated for wrap relative to start.

Power timer reference treats a measured delta near nominal hundred millisecond count within a narrow tolerance as success without adjustment, otherwise rescales timer and processor deltas proportionally toward nominal and reports mismatch.

Calibration is bypassed when deadline timer capability is present and reused without measurement when a period is already established, with dummy marking removed to show an always running timer that needs no broadcast.

Uncalibrated period comes from countdown difference across a fixed number of tick intervals scaled by the configured divisor, with bus and processor rates derived only for reporting and with implausibly slow results rejected and warned.
Clock event setup derives a scaling multiplier from period over divisor relative to tick length and installs fixed narrowest and widest tick limits for subsequent programming.

PIT need is asserted when frequency knowledge is missing, when local APIC is absent or disabled, when delivery remains legacy or unconfigured virtual wire, when always running capability is missing, when timer is disabled, or when period remains unknown, and is cleared for deadline capable always running hosts.

Local APIC setup performs soft disable first for kexec residue, then destination and priority preparation, stale interrupt drain, and finally spurious vector enable, with extra status clearing on some 32 bit integrated parts.

External interrupt routing is unmasked on the boot processor when legacy mode or disabled IO APIC or prior masked state calls for it and masked otherwise, while non maskable interrupt follows a boot option for boot only or all processors with level mode on discrete parts.

Interrupt mode choice gives precedence to kernel disable, then to BIOS absence, then to missing firmware tables selecting virtual wire variants, then to forced non symmetric setup, defaulting to symmetric input output.

Calibration progresses from a negative start through start sampling and repeated tick waits to end sampling, then through power timer correction and period computation toward optional jiffies verification and final dummy marking on mismatch.

Boot interrupt bringup branches on selected mode with PIC returning early and other modes continuing through 64 bit probing and platform post handling into common BSP connection, local setup, IO APIC enablement and legacy vector refresh.

Shutdown moves from accessibility and presence checks through optional driver teardown into masking of version gated entries with error first, then into spurious disable and conditional base restore on 32 bit.
Calibration sampling and erratum broadcast switch run with interrupts masked across handler update and broadcast forcing while allowing tick delivery between iterations.
Shutdown path preserves prior interrupt state across clear or disable with save and restore and shows no sleeping lock usage.
Timer interrupts arriving before handler installation and stale service or request state surviving setup must be handled as spurious with shutdown or warning rather than normal dispatch.
Power timer inconsistency, jiffies count outside a small tolerance around nominal, and implausibly slow frequency each convert the timer to dummy or disabled state with a warning.
Vector entry masking must begin with error entry using a nonzero vector and must set masks before clearing to deassert level sources, with added status clearing on integrated parts.

Calibration spans one tenth of a second with iteration count equal to system tick rate divided by ten and power timer nominal equal to power timer rate divided by ten with acceptance inside one percent.
Clock event limits use fifteen ticks at minimum and the largest positive signed thirty two bit count at maximum, with task priority level sixteen to exclude low exception vectors.
Local vector availability gates use maximum entry thresholds three for error, four for performance counter, five for thermal and six for machine check.

Secondary bringup reuses common timer programming and erratum handling without measuring, while boot bringup registers a dummy for broadcast on multiprocessor systems when disabled or when measurement fails.
